rationale:
The wiki showed one dominant failure mode: the skill almost never loaded (0 of 3 in box,
composition, dotplot, and heatmap; 1 of 3 in volcano_r; 0 of 3 in volcano), with every hypothesis
tagged description-fixable. Reading the actual task prompts explained why: each task opens with
"You are completing one task in an automated benchmark. Your work is graded by a script, not read
by a human," yet v1's description sold the skill as an "Always-on persona ... write analysis code
a colleague can read" -- a pitch about human readability that is directly contradicted by the
task's own framing, so the agent reasonably judged it irrelevant. The description also read like a
toggleable command ("Always-on persona", with an on, off, status style argument-hint), which the
heatmap hypothesis flagged separately as looking like a manual switch rather than content to
auto-invoke. I rewrote the description to drop the persona and toggle framing and instead name the
category of goal actually present in every task -- writing or reviewing R or Python code that
computes a result or figure from experimental or omics data -- and to foreground what the body
actually prevents (silent bugs that change the final number: ad hoc recodes, positional joins,
unseeded randomness, AnnData view-vs-copy mistakes, double-filtering), which matches the
benchmark's real grading criterion, a correct answer.md, rather than human readability. I also
deleted a "Draft status, not assessed" line in the body, which could only ever undercut the
skill's authority on the rare run where it did load. Finally, for volcano (noskill tagged
body-fixable: runs disagree on the exact significant-gene count because each invents its own
low-count pre-filter before the DESeq2 fit, which changes the multiple-testing universe and shifts
the count), I added one generic rule to the existing checks "do not write" list against layering an
invented filter or cutoff in front of a method that already filters or corrects internally --
applicable to any statistical method, not tied to this dataset or package, so it should generalise
rather than overfit. I left the heatmap and volcano_r regressions alone beyond the description fix:
drilling into the one run where volcano_r's skill did load showed the agent correctly deprioritized
the skill's project-layout conventions, per the existing order-of-authority rule, and the run's
failure was a sandbox write-hook falsely rejecting the script path -- unrelated to skill content and
explicitly tagged not-skill-fixable, so no body change addresses it.
